transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-10-23 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan H (Redwood AE), Priya M (Redwood SE), Eli N (Redwood CSM); Carlos V (ZenPath CTO), Leah K (Head ML Ops), Samir P (Infra), Nora B (Product), Maya O (Security)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align playbook, networking window, security checklist, and the pilot's first two weeks. Focus on latency SLO for real-time routing, cost allotment by team, and observability dashboards.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick round robin, goals, then Priya will run through the technical intake and we'll capture action items.
[00:12] Carlos: Hey, thanks. We're looking to get the inference pilot set up for our last-mile routing assistant, need sub-200ms p95 for short prompts, and want to keep costs under our current legacy baseline.
[00:25] Leah: And from ML Ops we care about model version pinning, rollback, and automatic quality regression alerts.
[00:33] Priya: Great, that's exactly what the playbook will cover, outlining the sandbox, traffic shaping, and observability hooks in Redwood Console — or as our docs sometimes call it, the Console dash.
[00:46] Samir: Quick networking thing — we need to know if you support cross-account VPC peering and what IP ranges we need to reserve.
[00:52] Jordan: Yes, we do. We'll share the peering window and guidance. Priya, want to take the intake?

[03:05] Priya: Sure, going through the technical intake — first question, are you leaning hosted or private? I know you mentioned regulatory constraints in the intake form.
[03:12] Carlos: We prefer Redwood Dedicated but want the option to move to Private in prod; during pilot we'll try dedicated reserved capacity.
[03:20] Priya: Ok perfect. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and simpler onramp, Private adds the VPC control plane and K M S integration. Note: K M S can be customer-managed in Private.
[03:32] Maya: On security, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and SAML S S O integration — S S O is a hard requirement. Also SOC2 report and a list of sub processors.
[03:42] Eli: We'll attach the security pack after the call; Priya can walk you through the log export options.

[06:00] Priya: For the model, what are you planning to serve? Do you have a base open model or a fine-tuned variant?
[06:08] Leah: We'll be running a fine-tuned L L M for routing heuristics — small context, typically 40-80 tokens per request, lots of concurrent short calls.
[06:17] Priya: That usage profile favors lower-latency kernels and continuous batching tuned to short sequences. We'll recommend a quantized variant to reduce GPU memory and cost. But we need to validate quality delta with your prompt set.
[06:29] Nora: We'll provide 50 exemplar prompts and expected outputs; that's on me.

[08:00] Priya: Observability — Redwood Console offers per-route P95/P99, token-level cost, and request traces. For your SLA we recommend alerting on P95 and error rate, and creating a canary rollout for model changes.
[08:12] Carlos: Can we get tracing integrated with our existing APM?
[08:18] Jordan: Yes, there are existing connectors, and we can forward traces asJa, as spans to your APM. There might be minor naming mismatches — sometimes the auto-transcript says the product as 'Redwood he seven' — ignore that.

[10:05] Samir: On infra windows, are there constraints for maintenance or auto-scaling? We have bulk traffic spikes at 03:00 UTC.
[10:15] Priya: We can configure autoscaling policies and burst capacity; you can set per-route limits to protect latency SLOs during spikes. Also, prefix KV caching may help for repeated queries.
[10:28] Leah: Tell me more about KV cache — is that prefix caching at the model runtime or upstream?
[10:34] Priya: It's at the runtime level — KV cache refers to key-value cache for transformer KV states between tokens, but we also have prefix caching to reuse identical preambles. Works well for repeated short prompts.

[13:00] Jordan: A note on cost allocation — we can tag requests by token groups and route metrics back to your teams. This helps show unit economics per product line.
[13:12] Nora: Good, we need that for internal chargeback.

[15:00] Priya: Pilot plan (weeks 0-2): set up sandbox in Dedicated, upload prompts, run synthetic traffic to measure p95/p50, iterate on batching/quantization, then run small canary on prod-like traffic.
[15:14] Carlos: What metrics do you want from our side?
[15:20] Priya: We'll need target traffic profile (RPS, distribution), sample prompt set, baseline latency and cost numbers, and a list of critical flows.

[17:30] Maya: Re compliance — will you support customer-managed certificates and integration with our K M S for encryption at rest?
[17:38] Priya: Yes in Private we support customer K M S; in Dedicated we can also integrate depending on the contract. We'll include the options in the security pack.

[20:00] Samir: For VPC peering, what's the typical IP plan? Do we need NAT or route tables configured?
[20:07] Jordan: We'll provide a template; usually you need a dedicated range and the peering is one-directional for control plane. For dedicated compute we can either peer or use a transit gateway. We'll document both options.

[22:40] Priya: On rollouts — we recommend canary 5->20% with automatic rollback on quality regression. Redwood Optimize can run quality monitors against a golden prompt set.
[22:52] Leah: How are regressions detected? Is it exact match or semantic similarity?
[22:57] Priya: You can choose metrics. We support token-level diff, BLEU-style metrics, and a lightweight semantic similarity score. We usually do a combination to reduce false positives.

[25:00] Carlos: Any limitations on model size for Dedicated?
[25:08] Priya: Depends on GPU type; we'll propose a sizing plan — typically we support up to multi-billion parameter models with quantization. For very large models we recommend sharded runtimes or Private deployments.

[27:30] Nora: For the sandbox, can we restrict access to just a product team?
[27:36] Eli: Yes, RBAC can be configured in the Console; you can map groups via S S O and limit route visibility.

[30:00] Jordan: Let's recap decisions: pilot on Dedicated, provide exemplar prompts, Redwood to send security pack, schedule peering window, and run initial synthetic test next week.
[30:18] Carlos: Timeline looks good. We're aiming to have the synthetic test by Oct 29.

[32:00] Priya: We'll also prepare recommended batching and quantization profiles for your short prompt workload. Expect that as a doc in 48 hours.
[32:10] Leah: Awesome. Also note we need to see audit log formats before we approve production access.
[32:18] Maya: Yes, and also an SLA addendum for Dedicated latency guarantees.

[34:05] Jordan: Action items noted. Any other questions?
[34:12] Samir: One more — can Redwood run a small benchmark with our sample queries? CPU vs GPU costs comparison?
[34:22] Priya: We can run benchmark harnesses in the sandbox; provide sample traffic and we will return a cost-latency spreadsheet. There might be slight variance due to quantization.

[36:50] Carlos: Do you have references for other logistics customers?
[36:55] Jordan: We can share anonymized case studies; we have a logistics playbook that outlines similar latency/cost tradeoffs.

[38:30] Nora: Quick note — I'll place exemplar prompts in the shared drive after the call and tag Redwood.
[38:38] Jordan: Great, we'll pick them up and schedule the cluster sizing session.

[40:00] Priya: Technical deep-dive follow-up: propose Monday 10am UTC for an infra workshop to size Dedicated cluster based on your RPS. Samir, does that time work?
[40:10] Samir: Works for us.

[42:00] Eli: I'll send calendar invites and the pilot playbook. Also attaching a quickstart repo for synthetic traffic.

[44:00] Carlos: Thanks everyone, excited to get this moving.
[44:06] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the pack and invites.

Closing notes: Confirmed next steps and owners in action items. Security pack and pilot playbook to be sent by Redwood; customer to share exemplar prompts and peering windows. Calendar invite for infra sizing workshop scheduled.

Transcript end.
